speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: When does vikalpa have use?
premises: yadā vikalpaṃ krameṇa saṃskurute — when the concept impresses in order.
samanantaroktasvarūpapraveśāya — for entry into the just-told nature.
bhāvanākramasya sattarkasadāgamasadgurūpadeśapūrvakasya asti upayogaḥ — the contemplation-sequence preceded by true reason/scripture/teacher has use.
inference: Vikalpa's use is conditional: sequence-impressed, triply-preceded (sattarka-sadāgama-sadguru).

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: How does vikalpa both bind and free?
premises: vikalpabalāt eva jantavo baddham ātmānam abhimanyante — by concept-strength beings mistake the self bound.
sa abhimānaḥ saṃsārapratibandhahetuḥ — that misapprehension obstructs saṃsāra.
pratidvandvirūpo vikalpa uditaḥ saṃsārahetuṃ vikalpaṃ dalayati — counter-pair concept tears the saṃsāra-causing concept.
iti abhyudayahetuḥ — hence prosperity-cause.
inference: The same instrument binds or frees: pair-opposed vikalpa dissolves the binding one.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is the concept that has crossed?
premises: samastebhyaḥ paricchinnasvabhāvebhyaḥ śivāntebhyaḥ tattvebhyo yat uttīrṇam — crossed all delimited Śiva-to-end tattvas.
aparicchinnasaṃvinmātrarūpam — undelimited-consciousness-merely-formed.
tat eva ca paramārthaḥ — that is the supreme truth.
tat vastuvyavasthāsthānam, tat viśvasya ojaḥ — place of thing-ordering, world's essence.
tena prāṇiti viśvam — by it he breathes the world.
aham ato viśvottīrṇo viśvātmā ca aham — world-crossed, world-self am I.
inference: Crossing yields the aham-identity: undelimited saṃvid IS paramārtha, the world's ojas and breath.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Who does not get this?
premises: sa ca ayaṃ māyāndhānāṃ na utpadyate — this does not arise for the māyā-blind.
sattarkādīnām abhāvāt — from absence of true-reason and rest.
inference: Māyā-blindness = absence of the sattarka-lineage; nothing else excludes them.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Why are Vaiṣṇava-type āgamas limited?
premises: vaiṣṇavādyā hi tāvanmātra eva āgame rāgatattvena niyamitāḥ — limited in scripture by passion-tattva only.
na ūrdhvadarśane 'pi tadunmukhatāṃ bhajante — even in higher vision no inclination.
tataḥ sattarkadveṣiṇa eva — therefore hostile to true-reason and rest.
inference: Passion-limitation breeds hostility upward: the Vaiṣṇava-type cannot turn toward sattarka.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What does Pārameśvara say?
premises: yathoktaṃ pārameśvare — as said in Pārameśvara.
vaiṣṇavādyāḥ samastās te vidyārāgeṇa rañjitāḥ — all Vaiṣṇu-and-rest colored by knowledge-passion.
inference: Cited authority: their color is vidyā-rāga, not neutral knowledge.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What do they lack?
premises: na vindanti paraṃ tattvaṃ sarvajñajñānavarjitāḥ — they find not supreme tattva, devoid of omniscient-knowledge.
inference: Deficiency stated: no sarvajña-jñāna, hence no parama-tattva.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Who enters the supreme own-nature?
premises: tasmāt śāṃbhavadṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhā eva — only those pierced by firm Śāṃbhava-descent.
sadāgamādikrameṇa vikalpaṃ saṃskṛtya — impressing concept by true-scripture-order.
paraṃ svarūpaṃ praviśanti — they enter supreme own-nature.
inference: Entry-condition: firm śaktipāta + ordered vikalpa-saṃskāra — both required.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Is parama-tattva then concept-form?
premises: nanu itthaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ vikalpyarūpaṃ syāt — but then would it be concept-form?
maivam — not so.
vikalpasya dvaitādhivāsabhaṅgamātre caritārthatvāt — concept's purpose is merely breaking dual-residence.
paraṃ tattvaṃ tu sarvatra sarvarūpatayā svaprakāśam — supreme is everywhere all-formed self-luminous.
na tatra vikalpaḥ kasyacit upakriyāyai khaṇḍanāyai vā — no service or refutation for anyone.
inference: Concept is soteriological tool, not metaphysical constituent: its work ends at dvaita-bhanga.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Who gets sattarka spontaneously?
premises: atidṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhasya svayam eva sāṃsiddhikatayā sattarka udeti — for the firmly-pierced, self-attained true-reason arises.
yo 'sau devībhiḥ dīkṣita iti ucyate — he is called initiated by the goddesses.
inference: Sattarka-arising = devī-dīkṣā: the spontaneous type is goddess-initiated.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What about everyone else?
premises: anyasya āgamakrameṇa — for another, by scripture-order.
savistaraṃ śaktipātaprakāśane vakṣyāmaḥ — with elaboration in power-descent-revelation.
inference: Two tracks: spontaneous (devī-dīkṣā) vs sequential (āgama-krama) — full treatment deferred.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Where does the sattarka-task actually lie?
premises: guror āgamanirūpaṇe vyāpāraḥ — task in determining the teacher's scripture.
āgamasya ca ... samucitavikalpayodaye vyāpāraḥ — and in fitting-concept arising from the scripture-chain.
tathāvidhavikalpaprabandha eva sattarka — that concept-chain IS true-reason.
sa eva ca bhāvanā bhaṇyate asphuṭatvāt — called contemplation too, from indistinctness.
bhūtam api artham abhūtam iva sphuṭatvāpādanena bhāvyate — existents contemplated as non-existent made distinct.
inference: Sattarka = chain-concept of fitting scriptural sense; bhāvanā = its indistinct-mode (making existent look non-existent).

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Do yoga-limbs serve as direct means here?
premises: na ca atra sattarkāt ... ṛte anyat yogāṅgaṃ sākṣāt upāyaḥ — no other yoga-limb is direct means apart from sattarka.
tapaḥprabhṛteḥ niyamavargasya ahiṃsādeś ca yamaprakārasya pūrakādeḥ prāṇāyāmavargasya — austerity/restraint/nonviolence/yama/retention/prāṇāyāma classes.
vedyamātraniṣṭhatvena ka iva saṃvidi vyāpāraḥ — what task in consciousness by knowing-merely-niṣṭhā?
inference: Limb-practices are object-level (vedya-mātra); sattarka alone operates in saṃvid.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Do the limbs still have a place?
premises: pratyāhāro 'pi karaṇabhūmim eva sātiśayāṃ kuryāt — withdrawal makes the instrument-level excellent.
dhyānadhāraṇāsamādhayo 'pi yathottaram abhyāsakrameṇa — meditation/concentration/samādhi successively by practice.
dhyeyavastutādātmyaṃ dhyātuḥ vitareyuḥ — they impart identity-with-meditated-object.
inference: Limbs are subordinate but real: they excellence the karaṇa-bhūmi and transfer tādātmya.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Can abhyāsa exist in parama-tattva?
premises: abhyāsaś ca pare tattve śivātmani svasvabhāve na saṃbhavaty eva — practice in supreme, Siva-self, own-nature is simply not possible.
inference: Practice presupposes otherness: in svasvabhāva it cannot arise — category-boundary.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is abhyāsa for the saṃvid-rooted?
premises: saṃvidrūḍhasya prāṇabuddhidehaniṣṭhīkaraṇarūpaḥ hi abhyāsaḥ — for the rooted, practice = fixing breath-mind-body.
bhārodvahanaśāstrārthabodhanṛttābhyāsavat — like carrying-load/scripture-knowing/dance-practice.
saṃvidrūpe tu na kiṃcit ādātavyam na apasaraṇīyam — in consciousness-form: nothing taken, nothing removed.
katham abhyāsaḥ — how then practice?
inference: Two registers: niṣṭhā-fixing (body-level) possible; saṃvid-level 'practice' is incoherent by definition.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Does reasoning (tarka) also do this work?
premises: kiṃ tarkeṇāpi iti cet — if asked: by reasoning too?
uktam atra dvaitādhivāsanirāsaprakāra eva ayaṃ na tu anyat kiṃcit — said: this is only the mode of removing dual-residence, nothing else.
inference: Tarka admitted only as dvaita-nirāsa-prakāra — instrumental, not constitutive.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is the meaning of abhyāsa even in the laukika?
premises: laukike 'pi abhyāse cidātmatvena sarvarūpasya — even ordinary practice as consciousness-selfhood of all-form.
dehādeḥ abhimatarūpatāprakaṭīkaraṇam — manifesting desired form of body-and-rest.
taditararūpanyagbhāvanaṃ ca — and contemplating other-forms' absence.
eṣa eva abhyāsārthaḥ — that is practice's purpose.
inference: Laukika-abhyāsa = cid-ātmatā-manifestation + anya-rūpa-nyāga — same structure, ordinary content.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is discarded in para-tattva?
premises: paratattve tu na kiṃcit apāsyam — in supreme tattva nothing is to be discarded.
inference: Apāsya is zero there: negation-work belongs to dvaita, not parama.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What exactly is dvaitādhivāsa?
premises: dvaitādhivāso 'pi nāma na kaścana pṛthak vastubhūtaḥ — not a separate thing-existing.
api tu svarūpākhyātimātram — mere own-nature-manifestation.
ato dvaitāpāsanaṃ vikalpena kriyata ity ukteḥ — hence rejection-by-concept, from the saying.
inference: Dvaita-residence is epistemic (ākhyāti-mātra), so its removal is vikalpa-work, not thing-work.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: How does paramārtha shine, and what follows for yoga-limbs?
premises: ayaṃ paramārthaḥ svarūpaṃ prakāśamānam akhyātirūpatvam — this paramārtha: own-nature shining as manifestation-form.
svayaṃ svātantryāt gṛhītam — taken by itself from autonomy.
krameṇa projjhya vikāsonmukham atha vikasat atha vikasitam — thrown-off, turned-to-expansion, expanding, expanded: by this order.
prakāśanam api parameśvarasya svarūpam eva — shining is the Lord's own nature too.
tasmāt na atra yogāṅgāni sākṣāt upāyaḥ — so yoga-limbs are not direct means here.
inference: The shining-order (projjhya-vikāsa) is svarūpa itself; limbs mediate but do not cause it.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is sattarka's relation to yāga etc.?
premises: tarkaṃ tu anugṛhṇīyur api sattarka eva sākṣāt upāyaḥ — even favoring tarka, sattarka alone direct means.
sa eva ca śuddhavidyā sa ca bahuprakāratayā saṃskṛto — sattarka is pure-knowledge, impressed in many forms: yāga, homa, japa, vrata, yoga.
tatra bhāvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ parameśvara eva sthitiḥ — there all states' abode is the Lord alone.
vikalparūḍhisiddhaye parameśvara eva sarvabhāvārpaṇaṃ yāgaḥ — for concept-conviction, offering-all-states to Lord = yāga.
hṛdyatvāt ... suśakaṃ parameśvare arpaṇam — from heart-nature, offering in Lord is easy; hence external flower/scent use.
inference: The five practices are sattarka's impress-forms; each = sarvabhāva-arpaṇa to parameśvara, externally scaffolded for heart-nature.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is homa here?
premises: sarve bhāvāḥ parameśvaratejomayā — all states made of Lord-light.
rūḍhavikalpaprāptyai parameśasaṃvidanalatejasi — for convicted-concept-attaining, in Lord-consciousness-fire-light.
samastabhāvagrāsarasikatābhimate — in all-state-swallowing-taste-desire.
tattejomātrāvaśeṣatvasahasamastabhāvavilāpanaṃ homaḥ — sudden all-states-dissolution-to-merely-light-residue: fire-offering.
inference: Homa = vilāpa into tejaḥ-mātra-avaśeṣa under the grāsa-rasa of Lord-consciousness.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is japa here?
premises: ubhayātmakaparāmarśodayārthaṃ — for arising of both-natured contemplation.
bāhyābhyantarādiprameyarūpabhinnabhāvānapekṣayaiva — by disregard alone of forms divided outer/inner-knowable.
evaṃvidhaṃ tat paraṃ tattvaṃ svasvabhāvabhūtam — this supreme tattva is own-nature-formed.
antaḥ parāmarśanaṃ japaḥ — inner contemplation: recitation.
inference: Japa = antaḥ-parāmarśana with bāhya/abhyantara-bheda disregarded — both-aspect contemplation.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is vrata here?
premises: sarvatra sarvadā nirupāyaparameśvarābhimānalābhāya — for gaining impersonal Lord-identification everywhere-always.
parameśvarasamatābhimānena — by equality-identification.
dehasyāpi ghaṭāder api avalokanaṃ vratam — viewing even body, even pot: vow.
inference: Vrata = samatā-bhimāna extended to pot-viewing: object-level equalization.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What authority for samatā?
premises: yathoktaṃ śrīnandiśikhāyām — as said in Śrī-Nandiśikhā.
sarvasāmyaṃ paraṃ vratam — all-equality the supreme vow.
inference: Cited: sarvasāmya is the para-vrata — authority for u25.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is yoga here?
premises: vicitraiḥ śuddhavidyāṃśarūpaiḥ vikalpaiḥ — by various pure-knowledge-portion concepts.
yat anapekṣitavikalpaṃ svābhāvikaṃ paramārthatattvaṃ prakāśate — what concept-independent natural paramārtha-tattva shines.
tasyaiva sanātanatathāvidhaprakāśamātratārūḍhaye — for establishment in being merely eternal-such-shining.
tatsvarūpānusaṃdhānātmā vikalpaviśeṣo yogaḥ — the specific concept of own-nature-tracking: yoga.
inference: Yoga = vikalpa-viśeṣa tracking svarūpa until the paramārtha shines concept-independently — self-liquidating instrument.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: How is parameśvara denoted in āgama-language?
premises: parameśvaraḥ pūrṇasaṃvitsvabhāvaḥ — full-consciousness-natured.
pūrṇataiva asya śaktiḥ — fullness is his power; kula, sāmarthyam, ūrmi, hṛdaya, sāra, spanda, vibhūti.
trīśikā kālī karṣaṇī caṇḍī vāṇī bhogo dṛk nityā ityādibhiḥ āgamabhāṣābhiḥ — by scripture-language names.
tadadanvarthapravṛttābhiḥ abhidhīyate — denoted running according to each sense.
tena tena rūpeṇa dhyāyināṃ hṛdi āstām — in each form let it be in meditators' hearts.
inference: Each āgama-name is an anvartha-projection of pūrṇasaṃvit — denotation is perspectival, referent one.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: How does pūrṇatā-consciousness shine?
premises: sā ca samagraśaktitādarśanena pūrṇatāsaṃvit prakāśate — by seeing whole-power-nature, fullness-consciousness shines.
inference: Darśana of samagra-śakti-tā is the condition of pūrṇatā-saṃvid manifestation.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: How many powers?
premises: śaktayaś ca asya asaṃkhyeyāḥ — his powers are countless.
inference: Countless in general; the structured twelve/four-counts follow as specific schemes.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Can the powers be taught?
premises: kiṃ bahunā — why say more.
yat viśvaṃ tā asya śaktayaḥ — the world: those are his powers.
tāḥ katham upadeṣṭuṃ śakyāḥ — how can they be taught?
inference: Rhetorical: world = powers = unteachable-as-list — sets up the counted schemes as approximation.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Which power completes the world in three?
premises: tisṛṣu tāvat viśvaṃ samāpyate — in three the world is completed.
yayā idaṃ śivādidharaṇyantam avikalpyasaṃvinmātrarūpatayā bibharti ca paśyati ca bhāsayati ca — bears/sees/illuminates as mere uncaricatured saṃvid up to Śiva-limit.
parameśvaraḥ — the Supreme Lord.
sā asya śrīparaśaktiḥ — that is his Śrīparā-power.
inference: Śrīparā = the triadic bearer-seer-illuminator in avikalpa-saṃvid-rūpa.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Which power works by difference-undifference?
premises: yayā ca darpaṇahastyādivat bhedābhedābhyām — by which, like mirror-elephant, by difference-undifference.
sā asya śrīparāparaśaktiḥ — that is his Śrīparāparā-power.
inference: Śrīparāparā = the bheda/abheda-relation power (mirror-model echoes a03).

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Which power works by difference alone?
premises: yayā parasparaviviktātmanā bhedenaiva — by self-distinct-from-each-other, difference alone.
sā asya śrīmadaparaśaktiḥ — that is his Śrīmadaparā-power.
inference: Śrīmadaparā = pure-bheda power, distinct-selfhood.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Which power holds the threefold in self?
premises: etat trividhaṃ yayā dhāraṇam ātmany eva kroḍīkāreṇa anusandhānātmanā grasate — by which the threefold is held in self by embracing, tracking-nature.
sā asya bhagavatī śrīparā eva — she is the Goddess Śrīparā herself.
śrīmanmātṛsadbhāvakālakarṣiṇyādiśabdāntaraniruktā — named by other words Śrīmat-mātṛ-sat-bhāva-kāla-karṣiṇī.
inference: Śrīparā double-duty: the triadic bearer (u32) AND the kroḍī-holder of the three — same Goddess, two functions.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: How do the four powers operate?
premises: tā etāḥ catasraḥ śaktayaḥ — these four powers.
svātantryāt pratyekaṃ tridhaiva vartante — from autonomy each operates threefold alone.
inference: 4×3 = the structure: each power triples by svātantrya.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What do they become?
premises: sṛṣṭau sthitau saṃhāre ca — in creation, preservation, dissolution.
iti dvādaśa bhavanti — twelve they become.
inference: 4×3=12: the twelve are the cosmogonic matrix (feeds u38's twelve Goddesses).

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is the twelve-fold saṃvit-kalana?
premises: saṃvit pūrvam antar eva bhāvaṃ kalayati — consciousness first constructs the state within.
tato bahir api sphuṭatayā — then outside by distinctness.
raktimayatāṃ gṛhītvā ... upasaṃjihīrṣayā — taking reddened-nature, intending reabsorption.
śaṅkāṃ nirmiṇoti ca grasate ca — forms and grasps the reabsorption-obstacle doubt.
grastaśaṅkāṃśaṃ bhāvabhāgam ātmani upasaṃhāreṇa kalayati — doubt-portion reabsorbed in self.
upasaṃhartṛtvaṃ mamedaṃ rūpam ... svabhāvam eva kalayati — constructs my-this-form reabsorber as own-nature.
kasyacid bhāvasya vāsanātmanā avasthitiṃ, kasyacit tu saṃvinmātrāvaśeṣatāṃ — some states habit-standing, some consciousness-residue.

karaṇacakraṃ ... karaṇeśvaram ... māyīyaṃ pramātṛrūpam ... saṅkocatyāgonmukhavikāsagrahaṇarasikam pramātāram ... vikasitam api rūpaṃ kalayati — constructs wheel, Lord, māyic knower, contraction-expansion-taste knower, expanded form.
etā dvādaśa bhagavatyaḥ saṃvidaḥ — these twelve Goddess-consciousnesses.
yugapat krameṇa dviśaḥ triśa ityādisthityāpi udayabhāginyaḥ cakravad āvartamānā — simultaneous/sequential, two/three-wise, revolving like-wheel.
māsakalārāśyādikrameṇa ... ghaṭapaṭādikrameṇāpi bhāsamānāḥ — by month/asterism order, pot/cloth order too.
cakreśvarasya svātantryaṃ puṣṇatyaḥ śrīkālīśabdavācyāḥ — nourishing the wheel-Lord's autonomy, denoted Śrīkālī.
inference: The twelve-fold kalana is saṃvid's full constructive cycle (in→out→doubt→reabsorb→knower-forms→expanded form), operating wheel-wise at cosmic and domestic scales — Śrīkālī is its name.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What counts as kalana?
premises: kalanaṃ ca gatiḥ kṣepo jñānaṃ gaṇanaṃ bhogīkaraṇaṃ śabdaṃ svātmalayīkaraṇaṃ ca — motion, throw, knowledge, counting, enjoyment-making, sound, self-dissolving.
inference: Seven listed operations define kalana's semantic range — construction includes motion and dissolution.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What do the Bhūtirāja-teachers say?
premises: yad āhuḥ śrībhūtirājaguravaḥ — as the Śrībhūtirāja-teachers say.
kṣepāj jñānāc ca kālī — from throw and from knowledge Kālī.
kalanavaśatayātha — by subjection to construction then.
inference: Cited: Kālī = kṣepa-jñāna pair under kalana-vaśa — authority for the kalana-encoding of time-power.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Where is this meaning elaborated?
premises: eṣa ca arthaḥ tatra tatra madviracite vivaraṇe — this meaning in my composed commentary here and there.
prakaraṇastotrādau vitatya vīkṣyaḥ — spread in treatise-hymn-and-rest, to be considered.
inference: Self-citation: the doctrine is distributed across Abhinavagupta's own vivaraṇa-corpus.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: How secret is it?
premises: na atirahasyam ekatra khyāpyam — not too-secret to be shown somewhere.
na ca sarvathā gopyam — nor to be hidden in any way.
hi asmadguravaḥ — so our teachers.
inference: House-rule: neither over-secret nor fully public — disclosure is graduated by context.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What follows for yāga-homa practice?
premises: yad uktaṃ yāgahomādi — what was said: offering, fire-offering and rest.
tat evaṃvidhe maheśvara eva mantavyam — in this kind the Great-Lord alone is to be thought.
inference: All ritual action re-presents maheśvara-only: the object of meditation during practice.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is the fierce argument about purity-rules?
premises: sarve hi heya eva upādeyabhūmirūpaṃ viṣṇutaḥ prabhṛti śivāntam — all see Viṣṇu-to-Siva as to-be-rejected ground-form.
tac ca mithyādarśanam avaśyatyājyam anuttarayogibhir — that false-view necessarily abandoned by unsurpassable-yogins.
tadartham eva vidyādhipateḥ anubhavastotre mahān saṃrambhaḥ — hence the knowledge-Lord's great fervour in hymn-of-experience.
yathā yathā bhavati tathaiva ācaret — as it becomes, so let him practise.
na tu bhakṣyābhakṣyaśuddhyaśuddhyādivivecanayā vastudharmojjhitayā kalpanāmātrasārayā svātmā khedanīyaḥ — not by purity-discriminations tormenting self by fancy-essence.
na hi śuddhiḥ vastuno rūpaṃ nīlatvavat anyatra — purity is not a thing-form like blueness elsewhere.
dānasyeva dīkṣitatve codanātaḥ — like gift's command in initiation.
codanāntare 'pi tulyam ... na śivacodanāyā eva bādhakatvaṃ — other-commands equal; Siva's-command alone obstructs.
yuktisiddhaṃ sarvajñānottarādyanantāgamasiddham ca — established by reason and endless scripture; we will say.
inference: Purity-rules are command-relative (codanā-vaśa), not thing-intrinsic; mithyā-darśana of heya/upādeya is what must go — the anubhava-stotra's fervour targets exactly this.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Do Vedic and other śāstra-restraints bind here?
premises: tasmāt vaidikāt prabhṛti pārameśvarasiddhāntatantrakulocchuṣmādiśāstrokto 'pi — from Vedic through Pārameśvara/tantra/clan/Ucchuṣma scriptures.
yo niyamo vidhiḥ vā niṣedhaḥ vā — whatever restraint, injunction, prohibition.
so 'tra yāvad akiṃcitkara eva — here it is of no effect whatsoever.
iti siddham — established.
inference: Radical scope: all hetero-scriptural restraint is akiṃcitkara within this system — only śiva-codanā binds.
